name: Faded Purple
lede: Faded Purple is ColorHub's name for Shion-iro (紫苑色), a traditional Japanese color named for the pale purple Tatarian aster flower.

sections.title: Shion-iro, the Tatarian aster
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Shion-iro, written 紫苑色, glossed as "Tatarian aster color" after the pale purple daisy-like flower *Aster tataricus* [1]. The Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan" is the only record we have for the name, and no book consulted for this project independently dates its coinage, so beyond that gloss it is undocumented here [1].

In LCH terms the library's swatch measures lightness 51, chroma 28 and hue 320 degrees, placing it in the Purples family [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dusty-violet]], [[dusty-violet]], [[aconite-violet]] and [[viola]], at 2.7, 2.7, 2.9 and 3.1 ΔE [1]. Two other library names nearby are [[opera-mauve]] and [[bishop-s-purple]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 2 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.01 percent, as photographed [2]. Both matches sit in shadow areas of the canvas [2]. The earliest dated appearance is 1869, in Eugène Boudin's *The mole of Deauville* [2]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor on the color's history, not a first sighting [2].
